newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: ONE KILLED AS BANGLADESH CRICKET FANS GO CRAZY.
newsitem.headline: ONE KILLED AS BANGLADESH CRICKET FANS GO CRAZY.

text.p: At least one man was killed and more than 100 injured in violence set off by Bangladeshi cricket fans celebrating the national team's semi-final win over Scotland on Wednesday in the ICC Trophy tournament in Malaysia.
Police said the unidentified man was fatally stabbed after he had abused fans spraying coloured water on passers-by in the Farmgate area of Dhaka.
More than 100 people were injured in a series of firecracker explosions and clashes between revellers and protesters in Dhaka and the port city of Chittagong, police told reporters.
Police said they had arrested at least 170 "mad fans" in Dhaka alone.

Win or lose in Saturday's International Cricket Conference (ICC) tournament final against Kenya, Wednesday's 72-run defeat of Scotland assured Bangladesh of a place in the 1999 World Cup in England, the first time the side has attained such heights.
On hearing the news, cricket-crazy Bangladeshis walked off the job and joined noisy nationwide victory marches.
Shouting students left class waving national flags to join street celebrations while government officials and office staff left work chanting "Victory for the Tigers".
Thousands of people marched in Dhaka and other main cities, witnesses said, amid exploding firecrackers, band music and paint being hurled in all directions.
"It's the biggest celebration since independence in 1971," said a journalist in the southern town of Khulna.
"We are seeing unprecedented jubilation everywhere," said a government official in the northern town of Rajshahi.
"It's colour and fun all around. This is something we never saw before," said journalist Mynul Hasan in the coastal town of Barisal.
Many girls caught up in the celebrations had to fend off enthusiastic boys chasing and touching them, witnesses said.
In Chittagong, home of Bangladesh team captain Akram Khan, hundreds of firecrackers exploded as state-run radio reported the last Scottish wicket to fall.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina had already promised each player a car if Bangladesh qualified for the World Cup alongside its powerful sub-continental neighbours India, Pakistan and reigning world champions Sri Lanka.
Telecommunications Minister Mohammad Nasim has now pledged a mobile telephone for every team member, and Health Minister Salauddin Yusuf has offered them free life-time medicare.
When Bangladesh failed to qualify for last year's World Cup, hosted by Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka, angry protesters took to the street overturning and burning cars.
